use_case_name: Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data

evidence_cards.content: IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) are transmitted in the J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages when available.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the core objective of exchanging IFF/SIF transponder data by specifying the message types used for transmission.

evidence_cards.content: The exchange of IFF/SIF modes and codes consists of five functional areas.

evidence_cards.content: The high-level objective of the use case is to summarize IFF/SIF message functions for surveillance data reporting, difference resolution, data updating, and clearing IFF/SIF data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This directly defines the goal of exchanging IFF and SIF transponder data as summarized in the table's functional categories.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to resolve differences between IFF/SIF transponder data received from remote units and the local unit's own data.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the objective of exchanging special codes, which constitutes a high-level goal for the C2 JU actor in the context of IFF/SIF data exchange.

evidence_cards.content: The Simulation Indicator in the J2 and J3 messages shall be set on all simulated tracks when both live and simulated tracks are simultaneously being exchanged on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a mandatory system state condition (Simulation Indicator must be set) that must hold before or during the exchange of IFF/SIF data involving simulated tracks; this is a precondition for valid simultaneous track exchange.

evidence_cards.content: Prior coordination with all interface participants is required when transmitting simulated tracks on the interface to insure that simulated tracks are not assigned TNs from other systems' TN blocks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a necessary pre-exchange coordination requirement — a precondition that must be satisfied before initiating transmission of simulated tracks to avoid TN conflicts.

evidence_cards.content: IFF/SIF data (Modes I, II, and III Codes) are transmitted in the J3.1 and J3.5 (PTI = 0) messages when available.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that availability of IFF/SIF transponder data is a necessary condition before transmission can occur; this defines a precondition for the exchange use case to proceed.

evidence_cards.content: The IFF/SIF data in the J3.1 message shall contain the IFF/SIF modes and codes of the previously reported track for which the emergency point was initiated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies that for emergency-point-initiated exchanges, the system must have prior track reporting context — a state that must hold before initiating such an exchange.

evidence_cards.content: The exchange of IFF/SIF modes and codes consists of five functional areas: a. IFF/SIF Surveillance Data Reporting (this paragraph), b. Unique Mode II Code Protection (paragraph 4.7.6.1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific functional areas that constitute the IFF/SIF data exchange process, which serves as a structural precondition for the use case execution.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must hold IFF/SIF surveillance data (specifically J3.2C1 and J3.3C1 words) for Air and Surface tracks to initiate the reporting exchange.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the existence of specific track data is a prerequisite for the 'Exchange IFF and SIF Transponder Data' use case to occur in the context of surveillance reporting.

evidence_cards.content: The JU must have IFF/SIF data locally held on the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: The text implies that holding IFF/SIF data is a state required for normal operation (transmitting periodic J3 messages), and its absence triggers specific behavior. This establishes the existence of local data as a precondition for standard exchange activities.

evidence_cards.content: The difference resolution matrix (Table 4.7-5) operates on 'OWN UNIT DATA' and 'REMOTE DATA' that are categorized by status such as 'NO DATA', 'VALID DATA' (subdivided into 'NON-CURRENT DATA' and 'CURRENT DATA'), or specific modes (e.g., 'MODE I OR III').
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific data states (preconditions) regarding local and remote unit data availability and validity required to engage the difference resolution logic defined in the table.

evidence_cards.content: Current IFF/SIF data are defined as those valid code responses that are no more than 40 seconds old since entry into the database by automatic or manual inputs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a temporal precondition for what constitutes 'current' data in the system before exchange operations can be considered valid under currency rules.

evidence_cards.content: Systems not maintaining currency indicators will assume local track/mode is current if remote IFF/SIF data is accepted in accordance with the difference resolution matrix (Table 4.7-5).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an implicit precondition state: when currency tracking is absent, acceptance of remote data via Table 4.7-5 triggers an assumption of local currency — which affects whether subsequent exchanges treat local data as current.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.5 (ACT = 2) message shall be manually initiated by R² and nonR² units with the applicable mode indicators set when requesting update of IFF/SIF data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that operator action is required to initiate an IFF/SIF Update Request, implying a precondition where the unit has identified a need for data update and the operator must manually trigger the request.

evidence_cards.content: Data updating can occur spontaneously as a result of the R² unit reporting a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report, J3.XC1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a system state condition (No Data status reported by R² unit) that triggers spontaneous data updating, indicating a precondition related to data availability status.

evidence_cards.content: The JU must have IFF/SIF transponder data available to exchange or have received such data from a remote unit.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the necessary system state (availability of data) required before the use case can begin.

evidence_cards.content: The exchange of IFF/SIF modes and codes consists of five functional areas: a. IFF/SIF Surveillance Data Reporting (this paragraph), b. Unique Mode II Code Protection (paragraph 4.7.6.1).

evidence_cards.content: The use case is triggered by the transmission of specific IFF/SIF messages (PPLI J2.0C1, J2.2C1, J2.3C1, J2.4C1; J3.XC1; or J7.5 with ACT = 0, 1, or 2) to perform functions such as surveillance data reporting, difference resolution, data updating, or clearing data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific message transmissions that initiate the functional exchanges described in the table.

evidence_cards.content: Specific triggers include operator actions, specifically for initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF function or a J7.5 (ACT = 2) Update Request.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Explicitly identifies 'Operator Action' as the triggering event for certain use case instances.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for surveillance data reporting is the condition where R² units hold IFF/SIF valid data locally for a track, or when any other JU (without R²) holds different data than the current report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific state conditions that initiate the reporting of IFF/SIF surveillance data, which serves as the start boundary for the exchange use case.

evidence_cards.content: The use case is triggered when C2 JU receives a J3 message that includes a continuation word with remote IFF/SIF data or a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message differing from locally held data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly defines the external event (receipt of specific messages containing differing data) that initiates the difference resolution process within the exchange use case.

evidence_cards.content: The use case is triggered when an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event (receipt of a conflict alert) that initiates the difference resolution flow within the use case.

evidence_cards.content: Data updating can occur spontaneously as a result of the R² unit reporting a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report, J3.XC1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific system-triggered event (No Data status report) that initiates the data exchange/update process.

evidence_cards.content: Data updating can also occur as a result of an operator action wherein the update request is transmitted in a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific user-initiated event (operator action via J7.5 message) that starts the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for exchanging IFF/SIF transponder data involves performing one or more of the following functional areas: Clearing IFF/SIF Data (paragraph 4.7.6.2), IFF/SIF Difference Resolution (paragraph 4.7.6.3), and IFF/SIF Update Request (paragraph 4.7.6.4).

source_locations.location: list items c, d, e and subsequent paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These are the core step-by-step actions that constitute the normal interaction sequence between C2 JU and the system for exchanging IFF/SIF data, directly defining the main_flow.

evidence_cards.content: The J2.XC1, J3.XC1, and J7.5 messages are used to perform the functional areas of clearing, difference resolution, and update request as summarized in Table 4.4-6.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exact message types used in the main flow steps, which is essential for describing the concrete interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for IFF/SIF data exchange involves transmitting messages (PPLI J2.0C1, J2.2C1, J2.3C1, J2.4C1; J3.XC1; or J7.5 with ACT = 0, 1, or 2) to perform functions such as surveillance data reporting, difference resolution, data updating, or clearing data. For example, PPLI messages are transmitted periodically with J2.XB messages, while J3.XC1 is transmitted at the next opportunity for new tracks when assuming R² or when data changes, and also periodically at 1/8 the basic message rate for realtime tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the core interaction sequence between C2 JU and other units via specific message transmissions that constitute the normal successful scenario for exchanging IFF/SIF transponder data across functional areas.

evidence_cards.content: When a J7.5 (ACT = 1) Difference Report is transmitted by nonR² JUs, it occurs when locally entered data changes from zero to nonzero or nonzero to another nonzero value, or in response to a J3.XC1 'No Data' report on one or more mode/code when local nonzero IFF/SIF is held. The system transmits this to report a difference in accordance with Table 4.7-5 IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix, and may be initiated by operator action anytime.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This details an alternative success path within the main flow where difference resolution is triggered by local data change or remote 'No Data' status, representing a valid variant of the canonical exchange scenario.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU may originate, by operator action only, the J7.5 (ACT = 0) message for the clearing of one or more modes on the specified track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an explicit operator-initiated step in the main flow for clearing IFF/SIF data via message transmission.

evidence_cards.content: All JUs, upon receipt of the J7.5 (ACT = 0) message, shall automatically set the designated mode(s) for the specified track to the No Data status; if accepted, this status is used for all subsequent interface functions and data link messages until updated by valid code responses from local or remote sources.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the automated system response and state update that follows the clearing message — a core step in the successful execution of the clear function within the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: A JU with R², upon receiving or initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message that results in no IFF/SIF data being held on the track, shall not continue transmitting the periodic J3 message that includes the continuation word containing IFF/SIF data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a behavioral constraint post-clearance: cessation of periodic reporting when no data remains — part of the canonical success scenario’s termination condition.

evidence_cards.content: Each JU without R² shall compare locally held data with IFF/SIF data reported by the JU with R² and report any valid data that are different... The JU without R² shall report current valid changes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the core interaction sequence for difference resolution — a key functional area under the use case — where non-R² units actively compare and report discrepancies as part of normal operation.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU receiving a J3 message that includes a continuation word with remote IFF/SIF data or J7.5 (ACT = 1) message differing from locally held data shall respond as indicated in Table 4.7-5.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the trigger-and-response mechanism embedded in the main flow for handling received differing data — directing the actor to follow a prescribed response table, which constitutes the next step in the interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for difference resolution involves comparing remote IFF/SIF data with own unit data using Table 4.7-5 to determine the action code (e.g., AT, AC1, AC2, NA, T1, TC) based on whether the remote unit has R² capability and whether its data is valid/non-current/current/local/remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This table defines the canonical decision logic and resulting actions that constitute the core interaction sequence of the difference resolution function within the use case’s main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When remote data is MODE I or III and own unit data is NO DATA, the system transmits AT (Accept Data and Transmit Received Data in a J3.XC1 word at next transmit opportunity).

source_locations.location: Table 4.7-5, row 'MODE I OR III' under J7.5 (ACT=1), column 'NO DATA' under R² UNIT

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a concrete step in the main flow: accepting and forwarding received data when local data is absent.

evidence_cards.content: If remote data is MODE II and own unit data is NON-CURRENT DATA, the system responds with C (Conflict — do not accept data and alert operator).

source_locations.location: Table 4.7-5, row 'MODE II' under J7.5 (ACT=1), column 'NON-CURRENT DATA' under R² UNIT

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception path triggered during main flow execution; however, since it results in operator alert and rejection, it belongs to exception_flow, not main_flow. Included here only to clarify boundary — actual main_flow claim focuses on successful resolution paths.

evidence_cards.content: In cases where remote data is VALID (MODE I OR III) and own unit data is NO DATA from a unit without R², the system responds with A (Accept).

source_locations.location: Table 4.7-5, row 'VALID DATA - MODE I OR III' under J3.XC1, column 'NO DATA' under UNIT WITHOUT R²

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Represents a standard acceptance step in the main flow when receiving valid remote data from non-R² units with no local data.

evidence_cards.content: When remote data is CURRENT DATA (MODE IV) from an R² unit and own unit data is also CURRENT DATA, the system responds with AC1 (Accept and transmit J3.XC1 word if upgrade; reject if downgrade).

source_locations.location: Table 4.7-5, row 'MODE IV' under J7.5 (ACT=1), column 'CURRENT DATA' under R² UNIT

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Illustrates conditional acceptance behavior based on upgrade/downgrade status — part of the canonical success scenario for resolving differences between current datasets.

evidence_cards.content: When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5, the following manual actions are available for attempting resolution: (1) Update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message; (3) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message; (4) Change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; (5) Decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing the assignment of a new track number to local data; (6) Clear operator alert.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This provides the specific step-by-step interaction sequence (manual resolution steps) that occurs after the trigger (conflict alert) is received, fulfilling the 'main_flow' requirement for the difference resolution functional area.

evidence_cards.content: In the IFF/SIF Update Request main flow: (1) The J7.5 (ACT = 2) message is manually initiated by R² and nonR² units with applicable mode indicators set; (2) R² units receiving this message respond by initiating a J3.XC1 message regardless of No Data status; (3) NonR² units receiving it from an R² unit respond by initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message if they hold valid local data (nonzero codes) for the requested mode(s), but remaining JUs need not respond if another JU already transmitted the requested data; (4) NonR² units receiving the J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from other nonR² units do not respond.

source_locations.location: Section 4.7.6.4 'IFF/SIF UPDATE REQUESTS', paragraphs describing rules a–d

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These steps define the canonical success scenario for operator-initiated IFF/SIF data updating via J7.5 (ACT=2), specifying actor roles (R²/nonR²), required responses, and conditions under which responses are suppressed—directly populating the main_flow slot.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for Surveillance Data Reporting involves transmitting IFF/SIF data (PPLI J2.0C1, J2.2C1, J2.3C1, J2.4C1) periodically with the J2.XB message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action sequence for the surveillance reporting functional area.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for Difference Resolution involves transmitting a difference report when locally entered data changes from zero to nonzero or nonzero to another nonzero value, or in response to a J3.XC1 'No Data' report on one or more mode/code when local nonzero IFF/SIF is held.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific interaction steps and triggers for resolving data differences.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for Data Updating involves transmitting an update request initiated by operator action via a J7.5 (ACT = 2) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the operator-initiated action sequence for updating data.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for Clearing IFF/SIF Data involves initiating the clear function by operator action via a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the operator-initiated action sequence for clearing data.

evidence_cards.content: For ID conflicts (where the difference cannot be automatically accepted or rejected), the system must present these differences to the operators for their evaluation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific step in the main flow for handling identity differences that require human intervention.

evidence_cards.content: Receipt of ID data on a TN for which the receiving JU does not have R² and local positional data is not held will automatically be accepted and the remote ID placed in the database for retention.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific automated acceptance step in the main flow for tracks without local data.

evidence_cards.content: For difference resolution of Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type and Special Interest Indicator, the C2 JU shall retain received values for retransmission and operator appreciation when accepting a remote ID change.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific action step within the main flow for resolving data differences during the exchange.

evidence_cards.content: When accepting a remote ID change, the appropriate evaluation of Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type fields shall be included in the J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific system response (message transmission) required to complete the difference resolution interaction.

evidence_cards.content: Differences in Environment/Category, ID, Platform, and other fields may also be resolved with the use of the J7.0 (ACT = 2) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative successful path (Change Data Order) for resolving differences, constituting part of the canonical success scenario.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for difference resolution involves comparing OWN UNIT DATA (REMOTE DATA) against R² UNIT or UNIT WITHOUT R² VALID DATA (LOCAL/REMOTE), resulting in actions such as ACCEPT (A), ALERT OPERATOR (AC), TRANSMIT J3.XC1 WORD (AT), REJECT DATA AND TRANSMIT LOCAL DATA IN J7.5 (ACT=1) MESSAGE (NT), or TRANSMIT LOCAL DATA IN J7.5 (ACT=1) MESSAGE (T1).

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the canonical interaction sequence for resolving differences between local and remote IFF/SIF data, including specific message transmissions and operator alerts that constitute the core exchange process.

evidence_cards.content: When a conflict is detected (C), the system does not accept the data and alerts the operator; when an upgrade/downgrade condition occurs under AC1, AC2, or AC3 rules, the system either accepts data with transmission of J3.XC1 word, accepts without action, or rejects data and transmits local data via J7.5 (ACT=1) message.

source_locations.location: LEGEND entries for C, AC1, AC2, AC3

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies conditional branching within the main flow based on data state changes (upgrade/downgrade) and conflict detection, which are integral to the difference resolution interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: If the same report is transmitted twice within 30 seconds during TC (TRANSMIT LOCAL DATA IN A J7.5 ACT = 1 MESSAGE) execution, automatic transmission of the J7.5 ACT = 1 message is inhibited and the operator is alerted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a temporal constraint and exception handling mechanism within the main flow that affects message transmission behavior and triggers operator intervention.

evidence_cards.content: When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the manual actions available for attempting resolution of the difference are: (1) Update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message; (3) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message; (4) Change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; (5) Decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing the assignment of a new track number to local data; (6) Clear operator alert.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific sequence of manual steps (main flow) an operator must perform when resolving IFF/SIF data conflicts, which is a core interaction within the exchange use case.

evidence_cards.content: Data updating can occur spontaneously as a result of the R² unit reporting a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report, J3.XC1. Receiving units which hold valid nonzero data will respond as required by the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix, Table 4.7-5.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the spontaneous initiation and response steps for the data updating main flow.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.5 (ACT = 2) message shall be manually initiated by R² and nonR² units with the applicable mode indicators set when requesting update of IFF/SIF data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the manual initiation step for the operator-initiated update main flow.

evidence_cards.content: R² units receiving the J7.5 (ACT = 2) message will respond by initiating a J3.XC1 message regardless of the No Data status.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific response action for R² units in the update request flow.

evidence_cards.content: NonR² units receiving the J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from the R² unit will respond by initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message if valid local data (nonzero codes) are held for the requested mode(s). If the requested data has been transmitted by another JU, the remaining JUs need not respond with their local data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the response action for NonR² units and the condition to suppress redundant responses.

evidence_cards.content: NonR² units receiving the J7.5 (ACT = 2) message from other nonR² units will not respond to the request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the interaction constraint between non-R² units during the update process.

evidence_cards.content: The originator of a J3.0 or J3.5 (PTI = 0) point, line, or area retains R² as long as the originator remains active and reports the point, line, or area.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the main flow condition for retaining reporting responsibility during IFF/SIF data exchange when using J3 messages; establishes continuity requirement for successful exchange.

evidence_cards.content: If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the R² unit is declared inactive, terminating the originator's reporting responsibility.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a termination step in the main flow where reporting responsibility ends due to explicit deactivation message receipt.

evidence_cards.content: If no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R² for the point, line, or area using the same Reference TN(s).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative path within the main flow where reporting responsibility transfers after timeout, requiring operator intervention — part of canonical success scenario under failure conditions.

evidence_cards.content: The latest IU to report on a reference or land (ground) point, line, or area has R² for the point, line, or area.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies the outcome state after transfer of reporting responsibility — defines who holds R² post-transfer, completing the interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: For Surveillance Data Reporting: PPLI J2.0C1, J2.2C1, J2.3C1, J2.4C1 IUs transmit own unit IFF/SIF data periodically with J2.XB message; J3.XC1 is transmitted at next opportunity for new tracks when assuming R² or when data changes, and periodically at 1/8 the basic message rate for realtime tracks and with each NRT track report.

source_locations.location: Table 4.4-6, Row 1 (PPLI) and Row 2 (J3.XC1), Column 'SURVEILLANCE DATA REPORTING'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the canonical transmission sequence for routine IFF/SIF surveillance data reporting as part of the main flow exchange.

evidence_cards.content: For Difference Resolution: J3.XC1 is transmitted at next opportunity after accepting or rejecting remote data received in J7.5 (ACT = 1) message; J7.5 (ACT = 1) Difference Report is transmitted to report a difference in accordance with Table 4.7-5 IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix, may be initiated by operator action anytime, and is transmitted only by NONR² JUs when locally entered data changes from zero to nonzero or nonzero to another nonzero value, or in response to a J3.XC1 'NO DATA' report.

source_locations.location: Table 4.4-6, Row 2 (J3.XC1) and Row 4 (J7.5 ACT=1), Columns 'DIFFERENCE RESOLUTION' and 'SURVEILLANCE DATA REPORTING'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the step-by-step interaction for resolving differences between local and remote IFF/SIF data, including triggers and transmission conditions.

evidence_cards.content: For Data Updating: J3.XC1 is transmitted at next opportunity in response to J7.1 (ACT = 1) Data Update Request and to a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request; J7.5 (ACT = 1) is transmitted in response to received J7.5 (ACT = 2) from the R² JU; J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request is initiated by operator action and transmitted by any JU.

evidence_cards.content: For Clearing IFF/SIF Data: J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF is transmitted by any JU and initiated by operator action.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the termination step for clearing IFF/SIF data via operator-initiated message, completing the exchange lifecycle.

evidence_cards.content: In the 'Difference Resolution' functional area, a C2 JU may elect to automatically accept changes in Environment/Category, Identity, or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific step/action within the main flow for resolving differences in IFF/SIF data (Identity) between local and remote units.

evidence_cards.content: When accepting a remote ID change during difference resolution, C2 JUs shall include the appropriate evaluation of Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type and Special Interest Indicator fields in the J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the required action and message type (J3.X/J7.0 ACT=1) for exchanging updated surveillance data as part of the normal flow.

evidence_cards.content: When accepting a remote ID change, C2 JUs shall retain the received values of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields for retransmission and operator appreciation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system response/data handling step following the acceptance of remote data in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: The C² JU with R² for the Reference TN shall respond with a J3.6 Space Track message upon receipt of a J7.1 message with the Data Update Request Action field set to value 2, Ballistic Missile Update Request, on a specific TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific response action in a data update exchange sequence involving C² JU, which is part of the main flow for exchanging surveillance-related data (though focused on ballistic missile context, it reflects structured response behavior applicable to IFF/SIF exchange patterns).

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the explicit exception handling paths available to the operator upon receiving a data conflict alert, which is the core content for the 'exception_flow' slot.

evidence_cards.content: Operator alerts may be implemented in individual JUs on an optional basis, such as alerting an operator whenever its data have been changed by accepting remote data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies an additional optional trigger condition for the exception flow related to data changes via remote acceptance.

evidence_cards.content: For Surveillance Data Reporting (PPLI/J2.XC1), the system state after successful completion is that IFF/SIF data has been transmitted periodically with the J2.XB message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable postcondition for the surveillance reporting function.

evidence_cards.content: For Difference Resolution (J3.XC1), the system state after successful completion is that data has been transmitted at the next opportunity after accepting or rejecting remote data received in a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable postcondition for the difference resolution function.

evidence_cards.content: For Data Updating (J3.XC1), the system state after successful completion is that data has been transmitted at the next opportunity in response to a J7.1 (ACT = 1) Data Update Request and to a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable postcondition for the data updating function.

evidence_cards.content: For Clearing IFF/SIF Data (J7.5 ACT=0), the system state after successful completion is that the action was initiated by operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable postcondition for the clearing function.

evidence_cards.content: For Difference Reports (J7.5 ACT=1), the system state after successful completion is that a report of a difference was transmitted in accordance with Table 4.7-5.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable postcondition for the difference report function.

evidence_cards.content: For Data Updating (J7.5 ACT=2), the system state after successful completion is that the update request was initiated by operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable postcondition for the update request function.

evidence_cards.content: For surveillance data reporting, the postcondition is that the JU with R² reports all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for a track in accordance with transmit rules; if no valid code is held (No Data), zeroes are reported in the applicable Mode Code field of the J3 continuation word.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system state (data reporting status or zero-filling) resulting from the successful execution of the surveillance data reporting function.

evidence_cards.content: Any change in IFF/SIF code values from No Data to Valid Data, or between Valid Data states, results in a report being transmitted as occurring.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the immediate observable outcome (transmission of a change report) when the use case successfully processes a state transition.

evidence_cards.content: Tracks with Valid Data which subsequently fail to respond to interrogations shall not be changed to the No Data status unless a Clear action is taken.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a critical persistence constraint on the system state (retention of Valid Data) after the exchange process completes, preventing automatic degradation to No Data without explicit clearing.

evidence_cards.content: Upon initiation or receipt of a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message, the system automatically sets the designated mode(s) for the specified track to a No Data status.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system state change (No Data status) that occurs after successfully executing the 'Clearing IFF/SIF Data' function.

evidence_cards.content: The interface returns to a No Data status for the specified track and its corresponding mode(s) when erroneous codes are cleared.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the resulting postcondition state (No Data) following the clearing action.

evidence_cards.content: Upon acceptance of a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message, the designated mode(s) for the specified track are set to No Data status, which is used for all subsequent interface functions and data link messages until updated by valid code responses.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the resulting system state (No Data status) after successfully clearing IFF/SIF data via the J7.5 message.

evidence_cards.content: A JU with R² that receives or initiates a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message resulting in no IFF/SIF data being held on the track shall not continue transmitting the periodic J3 message that includes the continuation word containing IFF/SIF data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the post-action behavior (cessation of periodic reporting) following a successful clear operation.

evidence_cards.content: The postcondition for a successful exchange where the remote data is an 'Upgrade' (under AC1) is that the system accepts the data and transmits a J3.XC1 word.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system state change (acceptance + transmission) resulting from a successful upgrade resolution in the difference resolution matrix.

evidence_cards.content: The postcondition for a successful exchange where the remote data is an 'Upgrade' (under AC2 or AC3) is that the system accepts the data.

source_locations.location: Table 4.7-5, Legend entries for AC2 and AC3

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the acceptance of data as the successful outcome for specific upgrade scenarios defined in the matrix.

evidence_cards.content: The postcondition for a successful exchange where the remote data is a 'Downgrade' (under AC1) is that the system rejects the data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the rejection of data as the correct successful outcome (maintaining higher quality local data) for a downgrade scenario.

evidence_cards.content: The postcondition for a successful exchange where the remote data is a 'Downgrade' (under AC3) is that the system rejects the data and transmits local data in a J7.5 (ACT = 1) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system state change (rejection + forced re-transmission of local data) resulting from a successful downgrade resolution under AC3 conditions.

evidence_cards.content: After successful resolution of an IFF/SIF data conflict alert, the system state reflects one of the following outcomes: local data is updated manually or verified automatically; a J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message has been initiated; a J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message has been initiated; local data has been changed to agree with remote data (except for Mode II code); local data has been decorrelated from remote data resulting in assignment of a new track number; or the operator alert has been cleared.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These are the explicit manual actions available to the operator that define the possible terminal states of the system after successfully resolving a data conflict — directly constituting postconditions of the use case when difference resolution is the functional area executed.

evidence_cards.content: Current IFF/SIF data is defined as valid code responses no more than 40 seconds old since entry into the database by automatic or manual inputs; however, systems need not time-tag IFF/SIF data for determining currency. When remote IFF/SIF data is accepted per Table 4.7-5, it is entered as valid noncurrent data. Systems not maintaining currency indicators will assume local track/mode is current if no indicator is maintained.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the temporal validity state of data after exchange — a key postcondition regarding data currency status that affects downstream interpretation and reporting behavior.

evidence_cards.content: After successful completion of the IFF/SIF Update Request (J7.5 ACT=2) functional area, R² units respond by initiating a J3.XC1 message regardless of No Data status; nonR² units respond by initiating a J7.5 (ACT=1) Difference Report if valid local data are held for the requested mode(s), unless the data was already transmitted by another JU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable system state after successful update request completion: specific messages transmitted (J3.XC1 or J7.5 ACT=1) based on unit role and data availability, which constitutes the postcondition for this variant path.

evidence_cards.content: After successful transmission of a J7.5 (ACT=3) Special Code Reporting message, the codes with special meaning for implementing JUs have been exchanged as intended by the message function.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the exchange of special-meaning codes via J7.5 (ACT=3) is complete upon message use — defining the terminal state for this functional area’s success scenario.
